sdk_correspondence.caveat: Spore-ModAPI is a third-party clean-room reconstruction, not original EA source and not EA documentation. Where it is cited below it supplies CANDIDATE NAMES only. The binary is the sole authority for every offset, constant, branch polarity and call shape asserted in this record.

semantic_contract: Returns the address receiver + 0x198 in EAX and returns. The receiver is read once, from ECX. The address is formed with LEA, so the result is the address of a member block inside the receiver, not a stored pointer, and callers may write through it. The block is three dwords wide (+0x198, +0x19C, +0x1A0), bounded from below by the setter at 0x00b8dae0. No branch, no callee, no global, no stack argument, no saved register, no virtual dispatch. The owning object is a Simulator::cPlanetRecord, established by the type-name literal 0x00ba61b0 passes to its allocator and corroborated by five consecutive field offsets in the Spore-ModAPI header for that class.
classification_rationale: STRONG_SEMANTIC on behaviour. The complete body, the ABI, the field offset and the absence of control flow, callees, globals and virtual dispatch are all read directly from the disassembly and from a live memory read, and they are corroborated three ways: by the setter at 0x00b8dae0 which bounds the block at three dwords, by seventeen callsites that read p[0], p[1] and p[2] as an identity triple, and by 0x00ba61b0, which constructs the owning object with the literal type name "Simulator/cPlanetRecord". No material uncertainty remains in the reconstructed behaviour. What remains uncertain is only the NAME of the accessor, which is a naming question and not a behavioural one; it is listed under unresolved_questions and the SDK correspondence is recorded as a candidate.
semantic_findings: The function is a pure constant offset: LEA plus RET, seven bytes, two instructions.
The returned block is three dwords, proven by the sibling setter at 0x00b8dae0, which writes +0x198, +0x19C and +0x1A0 from a three-dword source.
The result aliases the receiver, so this is a mutable-reference accessor rather than a const getter.
Callers treat the block as an IDENTITY triple, comparing all three dwords for equality against both incoming arguments and against the +0x64C triple of another class.
The owning type carries the literal type-name string "Simulator/cPlanetRecord" at 0x00ba61b0 and is allocated as 0x1B0 bytes.

Spore-ModAPI's Simulator::cPlanetRecord declares +0x184 mKey, +0x188 a ResourceKey, +0x194 TechLevel, +0x198 a ResourceKey and +0x1A4 a ResourceKey, and +0x2C int mFlags. Six offsets in that one header agree with offsets this binary reads (0x184 read and written, 0x188 address-taken, 0x194 read, 0x198 address-taken and three-dword-written, 0x2C bit 2 read). That is independent corroboration of the class, not of the accessor name.
Spore-ModAPI declares ResourceKey as three uint32 (instanceID, typeID, groupID), which matches the observed 12-byte block exactly.
The address appears in no data block, so it is not a virtual override; it is a plain out-of-line accessor reached only by direct CALL.
unresolved_questions: What is this accessor called in the original source? Spore-ModAPI declares mSpiceGen at +0x198 but no accessor for it, and declares GetGeneratedTerrainKey() for the +0x1A4 sibling instead. The names GetSpiceGenKey and SetSpiceGenKey used in this worker's reconstruction and filenames are this worker's invention, not SDK or original names.
Is the twelve-byte block at +0x198 a ResourceKey, three separate uint32, or a struct of three ids? The three-dword extent is observed; the field names are the SDK candidate's, not the binary's.

Spore-ModAPI's cPlanetRecord header is itself a third-party reconstruction, so the layout agreement is corroboration, not proof. The binary is the authority for the offsets; the header only supplies plausible names.
Is the block at +0x188, the second address-taken accessor at 0x00b8da60, the same kind of three-dword block? Its extent was not bounded; only its address was observed.
Does any caller write through the returned pointer, or do all 17 only read? Comparison sites were confirmed; a writing site was not searched for exhaustively.
Fifteen of the seventeen recorded callsites were not individually disassembled, so their receiver setup and result use come from the canonical xref list only.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists. A differential run must confirm the returned address is still receiver + 0x198 in the shipping build.
The class attribution rests on a type-name literal read at 0x00ba61b0. A run that dumps the concrete vtable pointer of a constructed record would confirm or refute it.
